Selling Surrogates

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A woman forges court documents to sell surrogates

Unique Selling Point:
Lee-Anne Strydom was a surrogate 6 times in 11 years herself before she opened her own agency, Destiny baby, which looked for surrogates for desperate parents
Her company has been operating since 2015. In 2017 she was taken to court for accepting a R5000 payment from commissioning parents for supplying them with a surrogate.

But what she was really doing was a lot worse. Elmarie Duplicay is a CT Lawyer, in 2018 she started noticing issues with court documents supplied by Lee-anne. In South Africa it is illegal to use a South African surrogate if you are not a SA citizen. The commissioning parents also have to have some DNA within the zygote. It is not illegal to use a surrogates eggs, but you have to validate the decision to do so in a court of law and get a judges permission to do so.
Lee-anne was supplying SA surrogates to international commissioning parents and forging the court documents stating that they were actually South Africans.
Besides the above she breached multiple laws with regards to Surrogacy:
No psychological evaluations were done prior to insemination
She told the surrogates that it was standard practice to use their own eggs
She told one surrogate that she would only get one zygote, as she was told she could not physically carry twins, but two were implanted and she had twins

When one woman's commissioning parents didn't want the baby anymore Lee-anne called the surrogate to say she had a buyer willing to pay 500 000 for the baby. The surroaget was horrified, as her eggs had been used she took the baby home and has raised it as her own.

There are 6 case studies and two willing to speak
One anonymous and one normal
Lawyer Elmarie has all the paper evidence and is willing to speak
She is a surrogacy lawyer.




Extra Budget Items:
Case study 1: Is in Bloemfontein. I think the best idea would be to bring her to JHB to do the interview instead of all going there. She is anonymous
Case study 2: Is in Heidelberg, she is willing to show her face and her child is with her so we can film there. Its only an hour away
Elamrie and Lee-anne are in CT

So it is 3 locations

Press Release:


Selling Surrogates
In South Africa it’s illegal to use a surrogate if you’re not domiciled in the country and without special permission from the High court. For many would-be-parents it’s an arduous experience so they often enlist professionals to assist with the process. Now Carte Blanche investigates how one woman, forged court orders so she could illegally sell surrogate services to desperate parents.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A woman forges court documents to sell surrogates
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Lee-Anne Strydom was a surrogate 6 times in 11 years herself before she opened her own agency, Destiny baby, which looked for surrogates for desperate parents Her company has been operating since 2015. In 2017 she was taken to court for accepting a R5000 payment from commissioning parents for supplying them with a surrogate. But what she was really doing was a lot worse. Elmarie Duplicay is a CT Lawyer, in 2018 she started noticing issues with court documents supplied by Lee-anne. In South Africa it is illegal to use a South African surrogate if you are not a SA citizen. The commissioning parents also have to have some DNA within the zygote. It is not illegal to use a surrogates eggs, but you have to validate the decision to do so in a court of law and get a judges permission to do so. Lee-anne was supplying SA surrogates to international commissioning parents and forging the court documents stating that they were actually South Africans. Besides the above she breached multiple laws with regards to Surrogacy: No psychological evaluations were done prior to insemination She told the surrogates that it was standard practice to use their own eggs She told one surrogate that she would only get one zygote, as she was told she could not physically carry twins, but two were implanted and she had twins When one woman's commissioning parents didn't want the baby anymore Lee-anne called the surrogate to say she had a buyer willing to pay 500 000 for the baby. The surroaget was horrified, as her eggs had been used she took the baby home and has raised it as her own. There are 6 case studies and two willing to speak One anonymous and one normal Lawyer Elmarie has all the paper evidence and is willing to speak She is a surrogacy lawyer.
